## Employee
- Name: Gandu (no id)
- Role: Instrumentation Engineer, Instrumentation
- Plant / unit: Haldia  / Unit 300

## Equipment history in the knowledge graph
- none found for this profile; interview from the profile alone and ask them to name their key equipment

topics.title: Unit 300 Instrumentation Landscape – Key Equipment & Unwritten Quirks
topics.rationale: No equipment records exist for this profile. The interview must start by having Gandu name the critical instruments he owns, then probe for undocumented behaviors.
seed_questions: Which 5–10 instrument loops or devices in Unit 300 would you say have caused you the most late-night calls?
Are there any transmitters or valves that have a 'personality'—where the reading is consistently offset or the positioner hunts—that everyone just works around?
Which piece of equipment has a history of intermittent faults that never got fully resolved?

topics.title: Undocumented Workarounds & Calibration Secrets
topics.rationale: Instrument engineers often carry calibration offsets, DCS force-points, or bypass routines in their heads that are not in any SOP.
seed_questions: Are there any instruments you routinely calibrate to a 'sweet spot' that differs from the manufacturer spec?
What DCS force-points or logic bypasses are currently active that a new engineer would never find in the documentation?
Is there a particular multimeter or communicator setting that works better than the book value for our environment?

topics.title: Critical Role Responsibilities & Daily Routines
topics.rationale: Understanding the informal scope of the role—what Gandu actually monitors vs. what the job description says—is essential for continuity.
seed_questions: Walk me through a typical morning round: what are the first three things you check that aren't on a formal checklist?
Which systems or alarms do you monitor out of habit, even though they aren't officially your responsibility?
What part of your role do you think management underestimates or doesn't know you do?

topics.title: Half-Finished Projects & Pending Modifications
topics.rationale: Retiring engineers often leave behind partially completed upgrades, trial installations, or uncommissioned loops that no one else knows the status of.
seed_questions: Are there any instrumentation upgrade projects you started but never fully handed over?
Is there any new hardware sitting in the store or installed but not loop-checked that only you know about?
What was the last modification you made to the control logic that is still running in 'temporary' mode?

topics.title: Vendor & Spare-Parts Tribal Knowledge
topics.rationale: Knowing which vendor rep to call, which spare parts are interchangeable, and which obsolete parts have hidden stock is pure tribal knowledge.
seed_questions: Who are your go-to contacts at Emerson/Rosemount/Yokogawa or our local rep that we should keep on speed dial?
Which 'obsolete' instruments do we still have a secret stash of spares for, and where are they kept?
Are there any non-OEM parts or third-party rebuild kits you've found that work better than the original?

topics.title: Early-Warning Signs of Impending Failures
topics.rationale: Experienced engineers recognize subtle patterns—slight drift, increased stroking time, noise on a loop—that precede a trip or failure.
seed_questions: What subtle changes in a transmitter's signal or a valve's response tell you it's about to fail, weeks before it actually does?
Are there specific weather conditions or process upsets that reliably kill certain instruments in Unit 300?
What is the one instrument you would preemptively replace before shutdown season, even if it looks fine on paper?

topics.title: Safety Instrumented System (SIS) & Critical Loop Gotchas
topics.rationale: SIS loops and safety-critical instruments have testing and bypass procedures where tribal knowledge of past trips and spurious actuations is vital.
seed_questions: Which safety instrumented function has given the most spurious trips, and what was the root cause you never fully documented?
Are there any SIS bypass procedures that require a specific sequence the written procedure doesn't capture?
What is the most dangerous instrument failure mode you've witnessed in Unit 300 that a new engineer should watch for?

topics.title: DCS & PLC Configuration Nuances
topics.rationale: Control system configurations often contain custom logic blocks, alarm rationalizations, or tuning parameters that exist only in the engineer's mind.
seed_questions: Are there any custom function blocks or logic sequences in the DCS/PLC that you wrote and only you fully understand?
Which control loops have tuning parameters you've tweaked over the years that would be lost if the controller were reloaded from backup?
What alarms have you intentionally suppressed or adjusted the deadband on, and why?

topics.title: Shutdown & Turnaround Tribal Knowledge
topics.rationale: Turnarounds have a rhythm and a set of unwritten rules—which instruments to isolate first, how to avoid damaging delicate devices during steam-out, etc.
seed_questions: What is your personal shutdown checklist for instrumentation that isn't in the official turnaround procedure?
Which instruments have been damaged during past steam-outs or chemical cleaning, and how do you protect them?
What is the one task during startup that you always insist on doing yourself, and why?

topics.title: Interpersonal & Cross-Department Dependencies
topics.rationale: Getting things done often depends on knowing the right operator, electrician, or planner. These relationships are invisible on an org chart.
seed_questions: Which operators in Unit 300 have the best instinct for spotting a bad instrument reading?
Who in the electrical or mechanical team do you rely on for tricky loop checks or valve overhauls?
Is there anyone in procurement or planning who 'gets it' and can expedite instrument orders when the system says no?

topics.title: Successor Advice & Open Risks
topics.rationale: A direct handover topic ensures Gandu can articulate the top risks he is leaving behind and what his successor must learn first.
seed_questions: If you had only one day to train your replacement, what are the top three things you would make sure they know?
What is the single biggest instrumentation risk you are leaving unresolved that keeps you up at night?
What documentation or drawing is so out of date that your successor should never trust it without field verification?

topics.title: Obsolete & Unsupported Instrumentation
topics.rationale: Older plants have instruments that are no longer supported by the vendor. The knowledge of how to keep them running is entirely in the retiring engineer's head.
seed_questions: Which instruments in Unit 300 are completely obsolete with no spares available, and how have you kept them alive?
Are there any 'black box' signal converters or custom circuit boards you've built or repaired yourself?
What is the one instrument you've been begging management to replace for years, and what is the consequence if it fails?

topics.title: Loop Drawings vs. Reality – Field Discrepancies
topics.rationale: Loop drawings and P&IDs often diverge from field reality over decades of modifications. The engineer carries the true as-built in their head.
seed_questions: Which loop drawing or P&ID in Unit 300 is the most dangerously wrong compared to what's actually in the field?
Are there any junction boxes or marshalling cabinet terminals that are mislabeled, and you're the only one who knows the correct wiring?
What field changes have been made over the years that were never red-lined on the official drawings?

topics.title: Environmental & Hazardous Area Instrumentation Challenges
topics.rationale: Haldia's coastal environment and Unit 300's hazardous area classification create specific failure modes—corrosion, moisture ingress—that are learned through experience.
seed_questions: How does the coastal humidity and monsoon season affect our field instruments, and what extra steps do you take?
Which Ex-rated instruments have given you the most trouble with certification or glanding?
Are there any instrument air quality issues that cause I/P converters or positioners to fail more often than they should?

topics.title: Emergency Response & Past Incidents
topics.rationale: Past instrument-related incidents and near-misses contain lessons that may not be in any incident report. This is critical safety knowledge.
seed_questions: What was the most serious instrument-related incident or near-miss you experienced in Unit 300, and what did we learn that was never formally written down?
During an emergency shutdown, what instrument behavior surprised you and almost made the situation worse?
If a specific alarm comes in at 2 AM, what is the first thing you would tell the operator to do that isn't in the alarm response procedure?
